narrative:
The 2017 Chicago White Sox entered the season in the midst of a deliberate rebuild, having traded away veteran pieces to accumulate young talent. April offered a deceptive glimpse of hope, as the club raced out to a 13-10 record behind timely hitting from Avisaíl García and a lineup that could still grind out victories. But the roster's limitations were always lurking just beneath the surface, and the departure of key trade pieces at the deadline would strip the team down to its developmental core.

May and June told the real story of where this franchise stood. The bullpen, anchored by arms that would soon be moved in trades, hemorrhaged leads at critical moments. Tommy Kahnle and David Robertson — both of whom would be dealt to the Yankees — were at the center of several gut-punch losses, even as occasional flashes from Tim Anderson, Melky Cabrera, and José Abreu reminded fans what this lineup could do on its best days. The month-by-month records of 11-18 and 11-16 reflected a team sliding toward irrelevance, even if individual moments like Abreu's clutch single against the Yankees on June 27 still stirred the South Side faithful.

July was the season's breaking point, both on the field and in the front office. A 6-18 record represented total collapse, and the trade deadline transformed the roster overnight — Kahnle, Robertson, Todd Frazier, and Melky Cabrera all departed, replaced by prospects. Yolmer Sánchez's walk-off homer on July 2 and Abreu's continued clutch hitting felt like farewell gestures to a contending era that never quite arrived. August brought more of the same losing, now against a backdrop of raw, unpolished youth learning on the job in the major leagues.

September offered a surprising and somewhat poignant coda. The stripped-down White Sox went 15-14, giving glimpses of the future in Yoán Moncada, Tim Anderson, and others who had been waiting in the wings all year. Rob Brantly's late-season home run in the final days was a small, symbolic moment — a backup catcher connecting for a pinch homer, a reminder that even in a lost season, baseball delivers its small joys. The 2017 White Sox finished 67-95, a painful but necessary step in a rebuild that the organization hoped would bear fruit in seasons to come.

chapters.title: A Deceptive Dawn
chapters.description: The White Sox jump out of the gate surprisingly competitive in April, with García's early power providing reason for cautious optimism.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Foundation
chapters.description: May and early June expose the roster's true ceiling as the bullpen implodes in high-leverage moments and the losses pile up.

chapters.title: Clutch Moments Before the Storm
chapters.description: Late June produces some of the season's most dramatic individual heroics, including Abreu's biggest single of the year, just before the roster is torn apart.

chapters.title: The Deadline Dismantling
chapters.description: A brutal 6-18 July coincides with a fire sale that ships out veterans and reshapes the franchise around its young core.

chapters.title: Growing Pains in August
chapters.description: The newly rebuilt roster struggles through August as young arms and inexperienced hitters absorb difficult lessons at the big-league level.

chapters.title: Glimpses of Tomorrow
chapters.description: A 15-14 September offers a hopeful final chapter as young players flash their potential and Brantly's late homer closes the book on a rebuilding year.
